evidence: Atomic layer deposition of titanium dioxide onto the mesoporous silica substrate was carried out in a homemade ALD flow reactor based on a reactor described by Elam et al.. Brieﬂy, samples were positioned near the center of a stainless steel ﬂow tube (3.5 cm diameter, 25 cm length) that was heated to a typical reaction temperature of 110 /C176C. Flow of the ultrahigh purity nitrogen carrier gas through the reaction chamber was maintained at approximately 30 sccm by a mass ﬂow controller. Electronically controlled Parker–General solenoid valves were used to accurately time the pulses of the TiCl4 and H2O precursors. Each ALD cycle consisted of an initial one minute exposure of the substrate to TiCl4 (flow of nitrogen was stopped and the flow tube was isolated from the pump during this exposure) followed by a 2 min purge of the reaction chamber to remove any residual TiCl4. The substrate was subsequently exposed to water for 30 s followed by a final 2.5 min purge of the reaction chamber.
